hypothesis_card.mechanism: AWS administers spot prices in infrequent large steps (capacity rebalancing, generation transitions, regional demand shifts); the trailing 730-day family change distribution mixes calm and repricing periods, so its empirical q90 sits below the size of a typical 90-180-day administered move when a repricing wave arrives. Pinball arithmetic: widening q90 by delta = (tf-1)*(q90-q50) costs 0.1*delta on the ~68-80% of cells that stay below q90 but saves 0.9*(overshoot) on the 20-32% breached cells, a net loss reduction; it also lifts coverage_80 toward the 0.80 calibration target (Gate 3). q10 is left byte-identical (h180 q10 breach is only 5.3%, widening there is pure cost) and q50 untouched so the center and the median-skill axis are not shifted by the width lever.
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery dry run: pooled 0.2716 vs champion 0.2675 (+0.0040, screen PASS), coverage_80 0.7031 vs 0.6640 (+0.039), q90 breach 24.6%->20.6%, h90 skill +0.0069 / h180 +0.0032, h30 byte-identical; median skill 0.2652 vs 0.2776 (-0.012, the known Gate-2 cost). Dense stride-14 backtest (33 origins): pooled delta +0.0062 (h90 +0.0072, h180 +0.0074), coverage 0.651->0.697, 54% of origins improved, helped cells concentrated in falling p4d AZs (euw1-az2 +0.0028, apne1-az4 +0.0022, use1-az1 +0.0018 contribution) where the q90 breaches lived.
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The rival explanation of the same errors: the +0.004/+0.006 gain is not tail under-dispersion but a generic coverage-buying trade that ANY unconditional widening scores in the 2023-24 Discovery window, whose rising-price regime produced outsized upper breaches; under it the Holdout (2025-03..08, a different regime with 116 late-starting series) would show the pooled gain vanishing while the median cost (-0.012 Discovery) stays or grows, i.e. Gate 1 or Gate 2 fails. Evidence partially against the rival: the dense stride-14 backtest spans both the 2023 rise AND the 2024-03..09 drawdown origins and the gain holds in both (helped series are the falling p4d AZs euw1-az2/apne1-az4/use1-az1, not only rising ones), and the widening is horizon-gated (h30 untouched, where breach was near target) rather than a blanket widening.
hypothesis_card.test: Paired dry run on the 16 Discovery origins (pooled +0.0040, screen PASS, would_reach_holdout=true) plus a dense stride-14 backtest (33 origins, 1530 cells) vs the champion: pooled delta +0.0062 with h90 +0.0072 / h180 +0.0074, coverage 0.651->0.697. Two rival levers were built and falsified first on the same harness: per-series x family blend (730d and 365d windows) -0.007/-0.026 Discovery pooled, family window 365d -0.019 backtest pooled, q50 shrink 0.8 +0.0008 (noise, z=1.3) — the tail widening is the only lever that cleared the screen.
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Falsified if the Holdout gates fail: pooled <= 0.2916 (Gate 1 = champion 0.2886 + 0.003), median < 0.2685 (Gate 2 = champion 0.2735 - 0.005; the -0.012 Discovery median cost is the explicit risk this episode accepts), coverage outside [0.70, 0.90] hard band (Gate 3), or any horizon skill < -0.020 (Gate 4). The under-dispersion mechanism itself is falsified if the Holdout q90 breach rate does not fall materially (>= 5pp) below the champion's while the pooled gain simultaneously fails to transfer (< +0.003) — that pattern would mean the Discovery gain was regime-dependent coverage buying, not calibration.

hypothesis: At 30/90/180-day horizons the champion's pooled 730-day family empirical change quantiles UNDER-DISPERSE forward administered spot moves: q90 is breached in 20.6% of h90 and 32.4% of h180 cells vs a 10% target (q10 breach 13.4%/5.3%). Widening the upper tail around q50 (q90_new = q50 + tf*(q90-q50), tf=1.25 at h90, 1.5 at h180; q10 and q50 byte-identical) is net pinball-positive because 0.9*P(breach)*overshoot >> 0.1*(1-P(breach))*delta at these breach rates, and it moves coverage toward the 0.80 target.
market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices at 90-180 days are administered in repricing waves large enough to exceed the trailing-window empirical 90th percentile 2-3x its nominal rate: dated evidence shows exactly such waves — CostPulse's AWS EC2 price-change feed for 2024-08-02 records 65,388 cuts AND 259,823 increases published in a single day (costpulse.io/aws-price-changes/amazon-elastic-compute-cloud/20240802172840/), LeanerCloud's 2024-05-03 review of EC2 spot pricing documents frequent multi-step administered repricing (leanercloud.com/blog/2024-05-03-thoughts-current-state-ec2-spot-pricing.html), and HPCwire 2023-11-08 reports H100 capacity buildouts pushing prices down in steps (hpcwire.com/2023/11/07/nvidia-h100-gpu-capacity-increasing-usage-prices-could-get-cheaper/). The champion's cross-sectional up-only reversion (below-median AZs pulled to the family median) assumes AWS keeps compressing spot discounts across AZs, consistent with the re:Invent capacity-management recap noting sustained spot price drops (zenn.dev/articles/831696491092b17). The upper-tail widening encodes the observation that these waves breach the trailing q90 far more often than 10%. The view would change if the market entered a calm regime with no repricing waves (widening becomes pure width cost, q90 breach < 10%), if a new GPU generation (p6/Blackwell) made current p4d/p5 capacity structurally cheaper in one direction (asymmetric breaches would then concentrate on q10, where the champion already under-breaches at h180), or if AWS stopped compressing cross-AZ discounts (the up-only reversion shift would misfire).
